data.title: A small resort that grew room by room.
data.intro: SandCove has 48 suites on a quiet bay. This page says how it started and what we do about the things guests ask us.

children.text: SandCove began in 2011 as fourteen rooms on an old coconut grove. Two families built it, one that had run a fishing lodge and one that had run a restaurant. They kept the trees and put the rooms between them.

Over the next twelve years they added the garden suites, the pool villas and the spa. The beach house opened last. Some of the staff who painted the first rooms now run the front desk and the kitchen.
What we do about the environment
We describe practices here, not certifications. We do not hold an eco label and we do not claim one.
Rain from the roofs is stored in two tanks and waters the gardens.
Water bottles are refillable glass in every room. We do not stock single-use plastic bottles.
Sheets and towels are changed every three days unless you ask for sooner.
The fish on the menu comes from two local boats, named on the menu board.
Garden trimmings and kitchen scraps go to the compost heap behind the staff building.
The reef is shallow and fragile. Guides ask guests not to stand on it or touch it, and we sell sunscreen that is free of oxybenzone and octinoxate.
The people

About 60 people work at the resort in high season. Most live within thirty minutes. Our general manager, Marisol Teague, has been with SandCove since 2013. You will see her at breakfast most mornings.
Visiting
The resort is quiet by design. There is no nightclub and no loud music after 10 pm. Children are welcome, and the shallow pool and the family rooms are near each other.

data.title: Three places to eat, all within a short walk.
data.intro: A restaurant, a beach bar and a long breakfast. Hours and sample dishes are below.

children.text: Allergies and special diets
Tell us about allergies in your request, or at check-in. Every menu has vegetarian dishes and most can be made vegan. Gluten-free and dairy-free versions are available on request.
The kitchen handles nuts, shellfish and sesame, so we cannot promise a space free of them. If an allergy is serious, speak to the chef before you order.

data.title: Resort policies
data.intro: Sample text. Replace it with your own terms before the site goes live.

children.text: Check-in and check-out
Check-in is from 3:00 pm and check-out is by 11:00 am. If your room is ready earlier, we will tell you. Luggage can be left at the front desk on arrival and departure days.
Cancelling or changing a stay
Dates can be changed or cancelled without charge up to 14 days before arrival. After that, the first night is charged. In December and January the notice period is 30 days.
Children
Children of all ages are welcome. Children under 12 stay free in an existing bed. Pools are not supervised by staff, and private pools are not fenced.
Pets
We cannot take pets. Service animals are welcome with advance notice.
Payment
A card is held at check-in. Nothing is charged by this website, and nothing is taken when you send a request. The rates shown here are sample rates.
Quiet hours
Please keep noise low between 10:00 pm and 7:00 am. The beach bar closes at sunset, or at 9:00 pm in summer.

data.title: Reef snorkelling
data.summary: A guided swim over the shallow reef at the north end of the bay.
data.season: All year, clearest November to April
data.intro: A guide swims with the group and points out fish, rays and turtles. The reef is shallow, so the water is rarely deeper than three metres.

9:00 am|Short briefing, then a boat ride of ten minutes
9:20 am|Snorkel in two stops with a rest on the boat
10:30 am|Back on the beach with fruit and water
data.bring:
Swimsuit
Towel (we also keep a stack on the boat)
Reef-safe sunscreen or a rash vest
data.provided:

Life vest if you want one
Water and fruit afterwards
